frozen_problem.title: Odd-primary Wood filtrations and a chromatic lower bound
frozen_problem.statement:
Odd primary analog of Wood cofibre sequences

The Wood cofibre sequence is the cofibre sequence $\Sigma \mathrm{KO} \xrightarrow{\eta} \mathrm{KO} \to \mathrm{KU}$ (and similarly for the connective versions). There is also a version relating $\mathrm{BP}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle n \rangle^{C_2}$ to $\mathrm{BP}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle n \rangle$.

What are odd primary analogs of the Wood cofibre sequence? For example, one might expect a $p$-stage filtration on $E_{p-1}$ with associated graded $E_{p-1}^{hC_p}$. Is there an analog for $E_{(p-1)p^{n-1}m}$?

theory.target: Certify the dimension-qualified regular-module criterion for residual cyclic p-group actions and expose failures when dimension or exponent checks are weakened; no topological realization.
definitions: k has characteristic p; q=p^n with n positive.
Rank-one regular means isomorphic to k[C_q], of dimension exactly q.
An orbit certificate is a basis v,g v,...,g^(q-1) v cyclically permuted by g.
assumptions: The field has characteristic p and q is a power of p.
g is a linear action with g^q=I; N=g-I.
Rank-one regular means isomorphic to k[C_q], hence dimension exactly q.
Residual representation certificates do not imply spectral realization, descent or Wood filtrations.
approaches_considered: Nilpotent top powers and the cyclic-vector independence argument.
Direct action orbits and modular elimination.
Weakened dimension or exponent tests, rejected by explicit block controls.
falsification_targets: A valid dimension-q action violating the top-power criterion.
A nonzero top power outside dimension q falsely accepted as rank-one regular.
A weakened exponent falsely certifying regularity.
Failure of a stored orbit-basis identity.

claims.statement: The exhaustive F2 dimension-2 and F3 dimension-3 census comprises 19699 matrices, 733 valid cyclic actions and 627 rank-one regular certificates; two methods agree, including nine specified block controls.
claims.falsification_condition: A missing matrix, invalid action, rank mismatch or failed cyclic orbit-basis identity.

claims.statement: The weakened dimension-free implication N^(q-1) != 0 implies rank-one regularity is false: over F3, N=J3 plus J1 has dimension 4 and nonzero square. This does not refute the dimension-qualified imported claim.
claims.falsification_condition: The displayed action fails g^3=I, has zero N-square, or actually has dimension 3.

claims.statement: Replacing the top-power test by N^(q-2) != 0 fails: over F3, J2 plus J1 has dimension 3, nonzero N and zero N-square, with no regular orbit basis.
claims.falsification_condition: An orbit vector spanning dimension 3, or an incorrect stated power.

claims.statement: For a characteristic-p field, q=p^n, g^q=I and dimension exactly q, the ordinary cyclic-vector proof gives rank-one regularity iff (g-I)^(q-1) != 0. Universal proof remains unverified by independent author or kernel.
claims.falsification_condition: Failure of the least-index independence argument, binomial basis change or a counterexample satisfying all hypotheses.

claims.statement: Carrick arXiv:2402.17519v1 Corollary 6.9 states the higher Real K-theory chromatic defect formula. Definitions 2.22 and 2.29 distinguish the p-local index and Wood type. No spectral realization follows from our matrix census.
claims.falsification_condition: Wrong source version or omitted hypotheses in the recorded limited background claims.
